label: Warden Merrow's first greeting — the treaty correction

purpose.value: Merrow greets the returning hero with wary courtesy and tries to correct his reading of the gates: nothing has ever come through them, and they are diplomatic doors proven by four thousand years of signed treaties.

emotionalProgression.note: An envoy's amulet earns a polite welcome; what she has filed from the Witness Glass earns the wariness.
She reaches for the treaty archive — her one move — and lays out what the gates actually are.
He thanks her for the intelligence briefing on enemy weaknesses and strides off; the courtesy held, the comprehension did not.

notes: Misunderstanding pair (Lore.md): she says 'They have never attacked us' and shows the treaty record; he understands 'my vigilance has kept them afraid' and hears the treaty read aloud as a war chant. She KNOWS the book is a children's comedy and may say so plainly ('filed under children's comedy, third shelf'); he hears 'a clever disguise over forbidden prophecy'. Never validate the hero's prophecy framing: there is no canon fact supporting 'the realms are evil', and that absence is itself the guard.
